executive_summary: Mathematical closure holds in the packet's own terms. For this 60-page, 982-item frontier the configured judge set returned complete verdicts across its 976-version verification scope; judge closure is closed with no open fatal rows; the 219 adjudicated claims resolved to 76 confirmed fatal, 115 confirmed nonfatal and 28 false positives; every fatal row is dispositioned fixed except one dismissed mislocated refuter; no fatal defect recurred; and no deferrals, terminal resolutions or workflow-owned blockers remain. The verdict is publishable-pending-owner-approval, and the remaining acts are the owner's: personal mathematical audit, deliberate status:published changes, and push/deployment. Residual risk is concentrated rather than diffuse: 76 of the 108 fatal rows surfaced only in Step-7 adjudication, 37 items absorbed two or more repair cycles, and churn clusters in the scheme-theory/algebraic-geometry, complex-analysis, differential-geometry and PDE material, so the priorities below target those places. All figures are as recorded in the packet; this report interprets them rather than re-deriving them, bound to evidence_sha256 f2082669c90ee0970fd3bf3632837fa50b514e5d0f3e30bd19a74b625e0662d3.
caveats: One of the 108 fatal rows is not a confirmed-and-repaired defect: frontier-36-complete-5a-b-hilbert-refuter-mislocated on thm-hilbert-polynomial-coherent-sheaf is dispositioned false-positive (a mislocated refuter), so the fatal-row count overstates confirmed defects by that row; the remaining rows are dispositioned fixed.

All closure verdicts come from the configured judge set: 1,163 version verdicts, complete with no null, mixed or incomplete rows. The packet contains no second rater's agreement data, so independent confirmation beyond that set is not evidenced here.

The by-subclass and by-location breakdowns describe the fatal rows only; the 115 confirmed nonfatal claims are counted in the adjudication summary but not itemized, so line-level audit of the nonfatal repairs needs the underlying defect ledger.

76 of the fatal items had already passed Steps 5-6 before Step-7 adjudication caught them (15 at 5a, 17 at 5b), so earlier-stage clearance is not evidence of sufficiency; audit late-caught items on their own merits.

The verified scope (976) is smaller than the built item count (982); the packet does not itemize the difference - coverage scoping is engine-owned - but it records complete verdicts for its scope and zero workflow-owned blockers.

Formatting-level observations, not content findings: repair_cost is 'unknown' on every fatal row, and build.items_by_kind carries one stray quoted "lemma" key (1) beside lemma (306), which reads as a tally artifact; unresolved in this packet, with no defect recorded for it.
